To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the noise figure and gain degradation with respect to room temperature are less than -0.1 dB and -0.3 dB, respectively, for a LNA operating at 10 dBm output power and 8-16GHz bandwidth.
the temperature dependence of the LNA performance can be accurately predicted by means of a noisy small-signal equivalent circuit.
the temperature has a strong influence on the LNA performance, and that a proper design is mandatory to achieve the required performance in the whole operating temperature range.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of low noise amplifier (LNA) for VSAT applications.
a detailed study on the performance of a pseudomorphic high electron mobility transistor (pHEMT)-based low noise amplifier (LNA) for Very Small Aperture Terminal (VSAT) applications.
the development of a new class of microwave transistors for VSAT receiver systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a 0.5-1 dB degradation in gain, a 0.2-0.3 dB degradation in noise figure and a 1-2 dB degradation in IIP3 are observed when lowering the temperature from 300K to 100K.
the performance of a pHETI LNA can be significantly improved in the VSAT receiver system by operating at low temperatures.

, in terms of noise performance, a LNA with a noise figure of 2 dB and an associated gain of 25 dB at 12 GHz is achievable at room temperature, while at 0 °C the noise figure can be further reduced down to 1.6 dB with a slight degradation of the gain down to 22.5 dB.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LNA design for the 8-12 GHz band is more suitable than that for the 13-18 GHz band, while a temperature of about 20-30 °C is preferable.
a low noise amplifier based on pHEMT devices is suitable for low noise and low temperature applications.
the LNA performance is mainly determined by the noise temperature and by the gain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the temperature dependence of LNA performance is not negligible and should be carefully taken into account in the design phase.
the noise performance of the LNA can be significantly improved by operating at lower temperatures.

, at least in the frequency band considered, the noise temperature of the LNA is not significantly affected by lowering the operating temperature, while the gain and power consumption increase, thus improving the overall receiver performance.
